title: Jazz education and students expecting favors
summary: Ridley says jazz programs teach cliches and Sam says black students expect favors as brothers.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well you know it's interesting to like in talking about it, this whole thing about what's happening to the thing. It's like even what's happening to the so-called jazz education. I've had to argue with people. I said, I told them 'hey look', with the people at the National Association of Jazz Educators, 'they think I'm crazy. They don't understand. I told them, I said, hey you all ain't playing no jazz. What you're going to get is essentially a concert band, you're going
to play some jazz cliches, you're going to call that jazz. That ain't playing no jazz man.

That's what I was telling them. I said, can you improvise. I said can you get up and just play a saloon? You all sit up and talk about that you know what's happening with jazz. You've got these kids, the first thing you ask some of them kids when they do some of them clinics, ask some of them kids what you want to play. "Giant Steps." "Giant Steps?" I said wait a minute, let's hit some blues right here. G-major right in there, just put it right in there. They'd be stepping all over it. That's the reason I'd be trying the same kind of thing that you were talking about as far as the black kids are concerned. Because the white kids are really trying to sap it up and they're doing it in so many different places. They're coming out and they feel like, they get little attitudes and the whole thing. I'm concerned about the black kids too to perpetuate this music. And that's the reason I'd be trying to talk to some of your constituents down there, trying to knock them duties on the side of the head, like old Carl and the piano player. What's his name? Alan. He'd be so busy trying to walk around here trying to act all hip and stay foolish and stuff.
That's the same thing I was trying to tell you, this is getting over man, you know trying to get around because you are black, you're the teacher. You are black so they figure
well he's my brother here. I don't have to study. I don't have to do this and I don't have to do that, because it's my brother here. I can see that he's going to let me...
